name: Question 7
worked_solution:
First, we factor the quadratic denominator, giving us the equation

$$
\frac{20}{(n-3)(n+3)}=\frac{3}{n-3}-\frac{4}{n+3}.
$$

We now make the following observations:

- The least common denominator of our equation is given by

$$
\text{LCM}(n-3,\,n+3,\,(n-3)(n+3))=(n-3)(n+3).
$$

- The values $n=-3$ and $n=3$ cannot be solutions to our equation. These values make at least one denominator in our original equation equal zero, and division by zero is undefined.

Now, multiplying both sides of the equation by the least common denominator, we can simplify it as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{(n-3)(n+3)} & =\frac{3}{n-3}-\frac{4}{n+3} \\ (n-3)(n+3)\cdot \frac{20}{(n-3)(n+3)} & =(n-3)(n+3)\cdot (\frac{3}{n-3}-\frac{4}{n+3}) \\ \frac{20(n-3)(n+3)}{(n-3)(n+3)} & =\frac{3(n-3)(n+3)}{n-3}-\frac{4(n-3)(n+3)}{n+3} \\ \frac{20\cdot \cancel{(n-3)(n+3)}}{\cancel{(n-3)(n+3)}} & =\frac{3\cdot \cancel{(n-3)}\cdot (n+3)}{\cancel{n-3}}-\frac{4(n-3)\cdot \cancel{(n+3)}}{\cancel{n+3}} \\ 20 & =3(n+3)-4(n-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation for $n,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & =3(n+3)-4(n-3) \\ 20 & =3n+9-4n+12 \\ 20 & =-n+21 \\ n & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $1\ne -3$ and $1\ne 3,$ we conclude that $n=1$ is a valid solution. 

Therefore, the solution to our original equation is $n=1.$

EXPLANATION

First, we factor the quadratic denominator, giving us the equation

20(n−3)(n+3)=3n−3−4n+3.

We now make the following observations:

  • The least common denominator of our equation is given by LCM(n−3,n+3,(n−3)(n+3))=(n−3)(n+3).

  • The values n=−3 and n=3 cannot be solutions to our equation. These values make at least one denominator in our original equation equal zero, and division by zero is undefined.

Now, multiplying both sides of the equation by the least common denominator, we can simplify it as follows:

20(n−3)(n+3)=3n−3−4n+3(n−3)(n+3)⋅20(n−3)(n+3)=(n−3)(n+3)⋅(3n−3−4n+3)20(n−3)(n+3)(n−3)(n+3)=3(n−3)(n+3)n−3−4(n−3)(n+3)n+320⋅(n−3)(n+3)(n−3)(n+3)=3⋅(n−3)⋅(n+3)n−3−4(n−3)⋅(n+3)n+320=3(n+3)−4(n−3)

Solving this equation for n, we get the following: 20=3(n+3)−4(n−3)20=3n+9−4n+1220=−n+21n=1

Since 1≠−3 and 1≠3, we conclude that n=1 is a valid solution.

Therefore, the solution to our original equation is n=1.
